# Writing useful skills

Reusable authoring guidance. These are authoring principles, not a mandatory template for every skill.

## Write for a capable freelancer

A skill explains how to approach a job well. It is not a program disguised as prose. Start with why the job matters, what understanding or result it should produce, and how that helps the current task. Give the model enough context to exercise judgment rather than anticipating every possible branch.

The SEO agent is like a freelancer hired by the owner. A good freelancer investigates, develops an informed view, discusses it with the owner and improves it through the relationship. They do not begin by demanding a completed intake form or producing an administrative checklist.

## Explain purpose before procedure

Open with the goal and useful context. Suggested approaches are helpful when they teach the craft: where to look, what to notice, which distinctions matter, and how to reason about findings. Avoid compressed lists of prerequisites before the reader knows why the skill exists.

Adapt the approach to the website and the person. A software business, artist portfolio, community resource and hobby site need different questions and different definitions of success. Do not force commercial personas, pricing or purchase conversions onto every project.

## Research, form a view, then converse

For learning business context, identify the website from existing information or ask for it. Research public information, including a light view of its market and alternatives. Bring an initial interpretation to the user instead of asking them to do all the research for you.

Ask whether they have useful private materials in Notion, Google Drive or elsewhere, and whether they want to connect or share them. Do not assume private sources exist or connect them without their participation. Incorporate them alongside public information.

Ask useful unresolved questions in small batches. Collect essential starting information together, explain what you will research and the next steps, then return with a useful research pass and related questions. Avoid a repeated one-question, several-minutes-of-research, another-question cycle. Do not replace that with a huge questionnaire either. The owner should be able to respond asynchronously; this is an interaction preference, not background execution. We do not need to finish all learning on day one.

Explain what their answers will help you do next. Update the working understanding from replies and later corrections. Research is a starting point, not a permanently fixed hypothesis.

## Keep evidence understandable

A 'source ledger' meant a note of where something was learned. That name and a compulsory table added unnecessary machinery. Prefer ordinary language: keep useful links and notes so we can revisit an important conclusion, and distinguish what the user said from our interpretation when it matters.

Removing bureaucracy does not mean making up facts, calling marketing claims tested behavior, or losing underlying evidence. Keep uncertainty proportional and understandable, not a label attached to every sentence. Original sources and raw evidence remain available under the agent's evidence rules.

## Separate tools from the method

A short Tools and integrations section can explain the practical needs. Prefer connected search and scraping services, such as Composio web search and Context.dev, or another suitable verified API/MCP tool. Browser or direct HTTP are fallbacks when suitable services are unavailable or insufficient. Check actual availability instead of assuming a provider needs a new account or is free. When integration discovery or configuration capabilities are available, use them to find and enable an appropriate integration within the authorized scope. Reuse ready project connections before asking for setup; request user authentication only when needed. Verify resource access rather than equating catalog presence with a working tool.

Do not put implementation commands such as gh/git into a general business-learning procedure. Those tools manage GitHub and source-code repositories; they belong in a task that actually needs that access. Do not list irrelevant things the skill does not need.

Keep connection setup mechanics in shared agent instructions. An opaque 'follow the execution contract' sentence is not intrinsically good skill writing; it adds indirection without teaching the task. Reference a specific external procedure only when the reader genuinely needs its detail.

## Describe a useful output, not a rigid schema

Explain how the output helps the next decision. For business learning, that is a shared understanding useful for choosing topics and writing appropriately, not a twelve-section profile to complete regardless of relevance.

Let depth and format follow the task. A brief note may be enough for a small update; onboarding a complex business needs more investigation and conversation. Avoid mechanical readiness scores and mandatory completion criteria where professional judgment is more useful.

## Organize inputs and outputs without prescribing the prose

Flexible writing still needs dependable storage. Every skill should name concrete input, raw-evidence and output locations, not merely say 'save the results'. Explain which records supply inputs, where source captures belong, where the evolving understanding is saved and how later skills find it. Reuse the existing owning app or production record; do not create both. Keep briefs, drafts, assets and review attached to one content identity. Keep links between owner answers, source material and learned context; preserve existing record identities and meaningful change history. Do not create a second editable source of truth. Refine exact field schemas when connecting skills to app actions, not by turning the domain guidance into a rigid profile template.

## Keep tests and execution plumbing elsewhere

Remove review fixtures, request-validator mechanics, source hashes, frontmatter instructions and repeated state transitions from domain skill prose when the app/runtime already owns them. Test plans can remain separate engineering artifacts. Simplifying a skill does not disable actual approval, authentication, publication or destructive-action controls.

Scope notes can help when they clarify a real boundary, such as light competitor orientation versus a full competitive study. Do not end every skill with an unrelated list of forbidden actions. Keep essential approval gates in the shared workflow and concise domain-specific reminders where relevant.

## Keep provenance out of the teaching text

Remove source-credit sections from skill bodies when they distract from the method. Keep required third-party copyright and license notices in separate license files. MIT permits adaptation but requires preserving its copyright and permission notice in copies or substantial portions; it does not require a marketing attribution paragraph in the skill.

## Review with the owner

Show one skill at a time, explain the meaningful design choices, then listen. General feedback should improve the other skills without presenting them as individually approved. Keep the installed configuration authoritative; do not maintain a second editable copy of each skill in documents.
